# Transformer-based Tomographic Reconstruction

Also called: SSTrans-3D, Slice-by-slice transformer network

## Overview
Transformer-based Tomographic Reconstruction is a deep learning technique that reconstructs 3D single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) images using a slice-by-slice transformer network (SSTrans-3D) [S1][S2, unofficial]. It addresses the considerable artifacts caused by incomplete projection data in image reconstruction [S1][S2, unofficial]. It differs from siblings like [DIOR](1409-dudotrans.md) by relying on a pure transformer architecture rather than combining deep learning with iterative optimization [S1][S2, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### SSTrans-3D
A specific slice-by-slice transformer network for 3D SPECT reconstruction [S1][S2, unofficial]. It is chosen when transformer-based approaches are preferred over CNNs or iterative optimization hybrids like DIOR to handle incomplete data [S1][S2, unofficial]. See [DuDoTrans](1409-dudotrans.md).

**Strengths and Limitations:**
Vision transformers were suggested to remove the restrictions of CNNs in image reconstruction, such as gradient-vanishing issues in very deep stacked layers [S1][S2, unofficial]. The method is compared against DIOR, which combines deep learning and iterative optimization to reconstruct limited-angle CT and improve generalization ability [S1][S2, unofficial].

**When to Use:**
Use when reconstructing 3D SPECT images with incomplete projection data and when avoiding the limitations of CNNs is desired [S1][S2, unofficial].

**When Not to Use:**
Not given in the sources.

## Background
The method belongs to a class of vision transformers suggested to remove the restrictions of CNNs in image reconstruction, where huge amounts of stacked layers can cause gradient-vanishing issues [S1][S2, unofficial]. SSTrans-3D is specifically applied to 3D single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) [S1][S2, unofficial]. It is compared against Deep Iterative Optimization-based Residual-learning (DIOR), which combines deep learning and iterative optimization to reconstruct limited-angle CT and improve generalization ability [S1][S2, unofficial].
